display_title: Cuproptosis-related IC candidates: expression, model comparisons and mouse follow-up
summary: The study prioritizes DLST, ATP7B, FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT through cardiac-expression screening and a four-model comparison. In a separate mouse experiment, LAD ligation was associated with higher DLST and ATP7B protein signals and lower FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT signals amid cardiac injury. The paper reports different sample counts and model-evaluation descriptions across source locations.
research_question: Which copper-related expression candidates characterize IC, how do their computational clusters and network contexts differ, and which protein directions recur in an injured mouse heart?
author_summary: The authors screen 19 cuproptosis-related genes, identify 14 differentially expressed genes and nominate five candidates for computational and mouse follow-up. The paper reports 203 ischemic cardiomyopathy profiles and 152 control profiles after merging two GEO datasets. Its consensus analysis divides the 203 case profiles into groups of 174 and 29. The four-model comparison reports its highest AUC for SVM (0.914). Three additional panels give AUCs of 0.933, 0.800 and 0.932, alongside differences in sample accounting and evaluation descriptions across the source. Inferred immune and pathway profiles, a 218-node ceRNA network and a 370-node chemical–gene network provide follow-up hypotheses. A separate LAD-ligation experiment shows cardiac injury and the same directions for the five protein signals as the human expression comparison.

study_profile.study_design: Retrospective public cardiac-expression screening, consensus clustering, CIBERSORT/GSVA, four model comparisons and additional ROC analyses; predicted regulatory/chemical networks and docking; separate sham-versus-LAD-ligation mouse experiment.
study_profile.evidence_type: Bulk-expression association, reported model estimates, inferred relative immune/pathway patterns, predicted molecular networks/docking and animal injury/protein measurements.
study_profile.population: Public cardiac-expression profiles from ischemic cardiomyopathy and control groups. The separate animal experiment used eight-week-old male C57BL/6 mice.
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Nomination and expression characterization of five cuproptosis-related IC candidates.
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Expression clusters, model and nomogram assessments, inferred immune and pathway patterns, predicted regulatory and chemical interactions, and mouse echocardiography, histology and protein expression.

key_findings.claim: Public expression screening and model-based selection nominated five cuproptosis-related IC candidates.
key_findings.context: Literature-derived gene screening followed by expression and model comparison in public cardiac transcriptomic resources.

evidence.label: Candidate screen
evidence.value: Nineteen literature-derived genes considered; Methods differential criteria |log2FC| > 0.5 and adjusted P < 0.05; fourteen genes described as differentially expressed.

evidence.label: Nominated set
evidence.value: DLST, ATP7B, FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT are the five candidates carried into the nomogram, network and mouse-expression analyses.

evidence.label: Bulk expression direction
evidence.value: In Figure 2A–B, DLST and ATP7B expression is higher in IC, and FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT expression is lower.

evidence.label: Reported merged analysis
evidence.value: Methods reports batch correction and merging of GSE5406 and GSE57338 into 203 IC and 152 control profiles.

evidence.label: Input-accounting difference
evidence.value: Figure 1 labels GSE5406 as 181 IC and 16 controls and GSE57338 as 91 IC and 136 controls. The inputs sum to 272 IC and 152 controls. The figure gives 203 IC and 152 controls after merging. The source does not describe the sample changes between those steps.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF p. 2, Methods §§2.1–2.2, p. 3, Figure 1, pp. 4–5, Results §3.1 and Figure 2A–B, and p. 7, Figure 4C.

key_findings.claim: Two expression clusters had distinct gene and inferred immune/pathway patterns.
key_findings.context: Consensus clustering within the reported 203 IC profiles, with CIBERSORT and GSVA analyses.

evidence.label: Cluster allocation
evidence.value: Cluster 1 has 174 profiles and cluster 2 has 29, with k = 2.

evidence.label: Cluster expression
evidence.value: Results and Figure 3 show higher LIAS, LIPT1, DLD, FDX1, DLAT, PDHB and DLST in cluster 1. NFE2L2, NLRP3 and ATP7A are higher in cluster 2.

evidence.label: Immune measurement
evidence.value: CIBERSORT estimates relative proportions of 22 immune cell types. Figure 2 shows IC versus control contrasts and correlations between gene expression and those proportions.

evidence.label: Main-text supplementary results
evidence.value: Results §3.2 reports higher inferred M1 macrophage and neutrophil proportions in cluster 2. It reports stronger oxidative-phosphorylation and myocardial-contraction pathway signals in cluster 2 and stronger mTOR signaling in cluster 1. The underlying supplementary plots remain unavailable.

evidence.label: Evidence role
evidence.value: Expression-defined heterogeneity and inferred immune/pathway context for candidate follow-up.

key_findings.source_locator: Original PDF pp. 2–3, Methods §§2.3 and 2.6, p. 4, Results §§3.1–3.2, and pp. 5–6, Figures 2D–F and 3A–G. Results cites Figures S1–S5 for cluster, immune and pathway support.

evidence.label: ROC estimates

evidence.label: Selection
evidence.value: The authors nominate DLST, FDX1, DLAT, SLC31A1 and ATP7B after the SVM comparison. Figure 4C displays ten feature-importance entries per model.

evidence.label: Evaluation wording
evidence.value: Figure 4D describes five-fold cross-validation in the testing cohort. Results describes differentiation between IC clusters, and Methods describes identification of IC. The exact fitted task and partitions remain unspecified.

evidence.label: Nomogram

key_findings.claim: Chemical–gene associations and molecular docking provide a computational comparison framework.
key_findings.context: Comparative Toxicogenomics Database associations and structure-based docking around the five candidate genes.

evidence.label: Network
evidence.value: 365 chemical entities and 5 genes form the reported network of 370 nodes and 615 edges.

evidence.label: Structure selection
evidence.value: The paper reports eight entries associated with all five genes. The vehicle-emission entry was excluded from docking, because the authors found no corresponding molecular structure.

evidence.label: Inspected heatmap
evidence.value: Figure 7B displays seven compound rows and five gene columns. The benzo(a)pyrene–FDX1 cell is −11.3 (kcal/mol, as stated in the Abstract). Figure 7C–G shows tretinoin docking poses for the five targets.

evidence.label: Naming difference
evidence.value: The heatmap labels one row Ethinyl Estradiol. Results §3.5 lists D004997 as acetoestradiol.

evidence.label: Scientific use
evidence.value: The associations and docking scores help generate hypotheses about chemical–gene interactions. The mouse ligation experiment had no compound-treatment arm.

evidence.label: Unavailable detail
evidence.value: Supporting Figures S6–S7 and Tables S2–S3 remain unavailable.

key_findings.claim: The ligation mouse model reproduced the nominated protein-expression directions alongside cardiac injury.
key_findings.context: A sham-versus-LAD-ligation expression experiment, separate from human model-performance and chemical-network analyses.

evidence.label: Allocation
evidence.value: Methods reports eight-week-old male C57BL/6 mice, allocated to sham thoracotomy or LAD ligation (n = 6 per group). The collection interval after ligation remains unspecified.

evidence.label: Cardiac injury
evidence.value: H&E and Masson stains show injury and fibrosis in the ligation group. Figure 8D shows lower left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening, and a larger left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (mean ± SD, n = 6).

evidence.label: Protein directions
evidence.value: Immunohistochemistry and myocardial Western blots show higher DLST and ATP7B signals and lower FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT signals in the ligation group.

evidence.label: Assay units
evidence.value: The Figure 8E caption gives n = 4 for GAPDH-normalized Western blots. The immunohistochemistry panel has no separate sample-size label.

evidence.label: Evidence role
evidence.value: The ligation comparison provides direct cardiac injury and protein-expression observations.

what_this_adds: Provides a concrete five-gene candidate set with public cardiac-expression context and separate mouse protein-expression observations.
Connects computational expression clusters and immune/pathway patterns with source-located model and nomogram comparisons.
Adds predicted regulatory and chemical-interaction maps that can inform follow-up experiments and comparison of evidence roles.

supports: The article-reported candidate-expression patterns and computational cluster/network summaries.
Exact published ROC values attributed to their panels and original sample/evaluation descriptions.
Mouse injury and protein-expression directions in the sham-versus-ligation experiment.
does_not_establish: A reconciled human sample map or frozen independent clinical diagnostic performance.
Gene perturbation effects or a direct experimental demonstration that these expression changes cause cuproptosis.
Chemical treatment benefit, measured molecular binding or a therapeutic ranking from the docking scores.

qa.question: Which five genes were nominated and what expression pattern was found?
qa.answer: DLST and ATP7B expression is higher in the human IC comparison, and FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT expression is lower. The authors select these five genes for the nomogram, network analyses and mouse follow-up after screening 19 genes and reporting 14 differentially expressed genes.

qa.question: What do the two molecular clusters describe?
qa.answer: The 203 reported IC profiles form two groups: 174 in cluster 1 and 29 in cluster 2. The groups differ in gene expression. Results §3.2 also reports differences in inferred immune proportions and pathway scores, including higher inferred M1 macrophage and neutrophil proportions in cluster 2.

qa.question: What four-model performance was reported?
qa.answer: Figure 4D reports AUCs of 0.914 for SVM, 0.911 for RF, 0.898 for XGB and 0.890 for GLM. The caption describes five-fold cross-validation in a testing cohort. Results describes IC-cluster differentiation, while Methods describes identification of IC.

qa.question: How should the additional AUC values be cited?
qa.answer: Figure 5D gives GSE42955 AUC 0.933 (95% CI 0.767–1.000). The Abstract instead gives 0.943. Figure 5E gives GSE48166 AUC 0.800 (95% CI 0.629–0.957), and Figure 5F gives GSE57345 AUC 0.932 (95% CI 0.892–0.965). The caption describes five-fold cross-validation within these datasets. The displayed Figure 5B is the decision curve, and Figure 5C is the calibration plot.

qa.question: Why are dataset membership and actual analysed samples kept separate?
qa.answer: GSE57338 deposits 313 unique GEO sample accessions, all present among the 319 in GSE57345. Figure 1’s two input case counts, 181 and 91, sum to 272, while the reported merged count is 203. Figure 1 also prints GSE5345 where Methods and the Figure 5 caption name GSE57345. The actual sample-selection map remains unresolved.

qa.question: What does the ceRNA analysis add?
qa.answer: The predicted network has 218 nodes and 264 edges, comprising 5 mRNAs, 52 miRNAs and 161 long noncoding RNAs. It proposes regulatory links around the five candidates, including associations involving LINC00969.

qa.question: What did chemical prediction and docking evaluate?
qa.answer: The CTD network contains 365 chemicals, 5 genes and 615 edges. The authors report eight entries associated with all five genes and exclude vehicle emissions from docking because a structure was unavailable. Figure 7B shows the benzo(a)pyrene–FDX1 docking score of −11.3 kcal/mol. Panels C–G show tretinoin docking poses. The mouse experiment did not administer these chemicals.

qa.question: Which observations came from the mouse experiment?
qa.answer: In mice with LAD ligation, histology shows myocardial injury, echocardiography shows lower ejection fraction and fractional shortening and greater end-diastolic diameter, and protein assays show higher DLST and ATP7B and lower FDX1, SLC31A1 and DLAT than in controls. Methods allocates six per group. The echo and Western blot captions report n = 6 and n = 4, respectively.

qa.question: Where can this work contribute to a research manuscript?
qa.answer: The work provides background on copper-related expression patterns in ischemic cardiomyopathy and a methods example linking public expression screening, model comparisons, inferred immune proportions and mouse protein assays. Cite the specific panel and dataset for a model estimate, and the actual mouse assay for an expression observation.

limitations: The Figure 1 input counts, its GSE5345 label and the Abstract’s GSE42955 AUC differ from corresponding values elsewhere in the paper. A sample inclusion and exclusion map is unavailable.

Methods frames the model as identifying IC and Results describes cluster discrimination. The reported cross-validation within additional datasets and the deposited accession sets leave the actual partitions and transfer procedure unresolved.
The animal experiment measures cardiac injury and protein expression. The regulatory networks and docking results supply hypotheses for a different experimental question.
Mouse allocation, echocardiography and Western blot sample sizes refer to different reported units. Post-ligation sampling time and selection for each assay remain unspecified.
Supplementary Figures S1–S7 and Tables S1–S3 were unavailable. The source locators distinguish the main-text descriptions from the supporting plots and tables.

related_papers.relationship: A separate pulmonary-hypertension study prioritizes disulfidptosis-related genes through expression, immune/pathway and model analyses followed by hypoxic-rat protein measurements. It offers a comparison of computational candidate selection and animal expression follow-up in a different disease and gene program.

provenance.version_of_record: International Immunopharmacology, volume 138 (2024), article 112574. Published online 6 July 2024.
provenance.evidence_basis: Original article, Methods §§2.1–2.14, Results §§3.1–3.6, and Figures 1–8. The official GEO records document the GSE57338 and GSE57345 accession lists.
provenance.source_note_accounting: Figure 1 gives input counts of 181 and 91 cases and 16 and 136 controls, and merged counts of 203 cases and 152 controls. Its comparison box prints GSE5345. Methods and the Figure 5 caption name GSE57345.
provenance.source_note_GEO: All 313 unique deposited GSE57338 GSM accessions occur among the 319 in GSE57345. The analyses do not provide an accession-level selection map.
provenance.source_note_model: The GSE42955 AUC is 0.933 in Figure 5D and 0.943 in the Abstract. Figure 5B is the decision curve and Figure 5C is the calibration plot. The reported fitted task and evaluation partition remain unclear.
provenance.source_note_network: The last sentence of Results §3.4 prints ATP3B. The nominated gene list and the Figure 6 network node identify ATP7B.
provenance.source_note_chemicals: Figure 7B labels Ethinyl Estradiol, while Results §3.5 calls D004997 acetoestradiol. The docking analysis is separate from the mouse ligation experiment.
provenance.source_note_supplements: Appendix A points to the publication DOI for supplementary material. Figures S1–S7 and Tables S1–S3 remain unavailable. The article text reports some of their results.
provenance.source_note_animal: Methods allocates six mice per group. The echocardiography caption gives n = 6 and the Western blot caption n = 4. The IHC sample size and post-ligation collection interval are unspecified.
